title: Gating & prioritization playbook for reserved throughput: burst credits, GPU affinity, and tail-latency SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we scale Dedicated offerings to enterprise customers we get requests that vary widely: strict p99 tail-latency SLAs, sporadic but massive burst needs, or throughput commitments that must map to specific GPU classes. Current intake is ad-hoc, causing under/overprovisioning and long negotiation cycles.

Goal: Create a deterministic triage/playbook that gates incoming reserved-throughput requests, recommends GPU class and burst policies, and produces an outcome: (Accept w/standard SLA), (Accept w/ Burst Credits & Guardrails), (Pilot on Trial Pool), or (Refer to Dedicated Solutions). The playbook must be operationalizable in the intake form and documented for sales/CS/solutions engineering.

Scope: Enterprise dedicated capacity requests (non-bug feature requests). Focus on: SLA targets (latency p50/p95/p99), reserved throughput and burst patterns, GPU family affinity (A100/H100/L4/other), preemption and graceful degradation policies, and billing/commitment constructs (burst credits, buffer pools). Non-goals: deep scheduling implementation, kernel selection, or infra-level autoscaling algorithms (these will be coord with ENG teams).
intake_fields: Peak burst RPS and burst window (e.g., 10k rps for 60s)
Request mix (generation / embeddings / reranking) and percent distribution
Cost sensitivity (low/medium/high) and expected commitment length
Must-have features: KV cache reuse, streaming, tool-calls
Can traffic degrade to lower-quality variants on overload? (yes/no)
Preferred rollout cadence and pilot window
prioritization_rubric: Revenue impact (0-5): committed ARR tied to reserved capacity
Latency criticality (0-5): sub-200ms p95 vs best-effort
Burst risk (0-5): freq and magnitude of bursts relative to steady-state
Engineering integration cost (0-5): custom networking/KMS/agent work
Fit for reserved (0-5): predictability of baseline vs transient spikes
Strategic value (0-5): reference customer, sector expansion
decision_matrix:
Score = weighted sum (Revenue*3 + Latency*2 + Regulatory*3 + Burst*1 + EngCost*-1 + Fit*2 + Strategic*2). Outcome mapping: Score >= 40 -> Accept: provision reserved pool + negotiate burst credit bucket; 28-39 -> Pilot on Trial Pool + require additional telemetry for 90 days; 15-27 -> Conditional Accept (must reduce SLOs or pay for dedicated burst window); <15 -> Defer to self-serve guidance or recommend hosted API.

GPU affinity guidance (heuristic): FP16/FP32 heavy gen models -> H100 preferred for p99 <250ms at high concurrency; A100 or equivalent -> balanced throughput/cost; L4/edge accelerators -> embedding-heavy or quantized int8 models where latency budgets are looser. Include fallback mapping for quantized variants and best-effort preemption buckets.
rollout_steps: Draft intake form fields (this ticket) and embed in internal portal
Implement scoring engine as spreadsheet prototype and test with 10 historical intake records
Workshop with Solutions Eng and Sales (wk of 2026-03-15) to iterate thresholds
Produce recommended GPU affinity matrix and burst-credit definitions for ENG
Add recommended default policies to Console: burst credit purchase flow + guardrail templates
Pilot with two customers (one latency-sensitive, one bursty) and collect telemetry for 90 days
Formalize SLA wording and billing terms with Legal and Finance
acceptance_criteria: Intake form implemented and accessible to Sales/CS
Scoring prototype validated against 10 past requests with documented outcomes
GPU affinity guidance reviewed and signed off by Infra/RE/Serving runtime leads
At least one pilot customer onboarded to the trial pool with telemetry dashboards
Billing & contract language for burst credits drafted and approved by Finance/Legal
